chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakaria al-Qattan narrated to us, from Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, from Tamim ibn Buhlool, who said: Abu Muawiyah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, who said: I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) say:

God has not burdened the servants except with less than what they can bear. He has only required of them five prayers in the day and night; He has required of them twenty-five dirhams for every one thousand dirhams; He has required of them fasting for thirty days in the year; and He has required of them one Hajj pilgrimage, while they are capable of more than that.

The compiler of this book, may God be pleased with him, said: The view of the special ones of the Shi'a and those of insight among them regarding the month of Ramadan is that it never falls short of thirty days. The narrations in this regard agree with the Book (Quran) and contradict the general public. Those among the weak of the Shi'a who followed the narrations that came for Taqiyya (concealment) stating that it decreases and is affected by the months' deficiency and fullness, have been cautious like the general public, and were spoken to only as the general public is spoken to. And there is no power except with God.

key_terms.خَمْسَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ دِرْهَمًا: Twenty-five dirhams (referring to 2.5% Zakat on 1000 dirhams)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on the length of Ramadan and how does it relate to Taqiyya?
ai.summary: Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the principle of divine ease by citing the five daily prayers, 2.5% Zakat, thirty days of fasting, and a single Hajj as obligations well within human capacity. Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this by noting that while the Shi'a scholarly consensus holds Ramadan as strictly thirty days, some adherents adopted the variable twenty-nine/thirty-day view for Taqiyya to align with the general public's practice.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 21-8 Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Qat’tan narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakaria al-Qat’tan quoted Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Tamim ibn Buhlool, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Mihran that he had heard Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB)say,

“I swear by God that God has not placed a burden on His servants more than they can bear. He has only required that they pray five times each day and night; has established only twenty-five Dirhams of alms-tax for each one-thousand Dirhams; has only required them to fast for thirty days during a year; and has only required them to go on the Hajj pilgrimage once in their lifetime.”

The compiler of the book - may God be pleased with him - said, “The Shiites and their wise men consider Ramazan as never being less than thirty days. The narrations which have been written in this chapter are in agreement with the Quran but against the public opinion (that sometimes the month of Ramazan may be less than thirty days). Those people with little faith in the Shiites who have maintained that Ramazan is thirty days every now and then, and twenty-nine days every now and then, have resorted to the concealment of faith. They have supported the general viewpoint of the public. There is no power nor any strength but in God.”
